newsitem.title: USA: Saudi oil minister warns against tight inventories.
newsitem.headline: Saudi oil minister warns against tight inventories.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Oil Minister Ali Naimi Monday warned attendees at a meeting of the American Petroleum Institute the oil industry's trend toward keeping leaner inventories could be "penny-wise and pound-foolish."

"In any market, shortfalls in supply affect prices and spur measures to quickly restore balance. While we can appreciate the increasingly competitive nature of our business, we also question how far should just-in-time inventory go to minimize cost," Naimi said.
"When all is said and done, such efforts may end up being penny-wise and pound-foolish," he said.
The Saudi oil minister declined to make any comment about current prices or the likely outcome of the upcoming OPEC meeting which starts in two weeks.
But Naimi said the world oil market was becoming increasingly sensitive to regional developments such as a shortfall of supply in the United States.

"If projections fail to match actual demand, as we have recently seen in oil distillates, the result is price spikes and unsettling reaction from the market. One has to wonder, then, about the validity of bringing oil stocks to precariously low levels," he said.
The minister indicated that the futures market might have a role in increasing volatility of prices, but he said he also saw benefits.
"The futures market does have some shortcomings and it attracts speculators. But it has created tools like hedging, which may aid some consumers and producers," he said
Many OPEC members have long criticized the futures market as one of the main reasons for oil price instability.
